google.summary: A polarised listing rather than a uniformly warm one: 71 of the 75 reviews are five stars, the other four are one or two. Most of the volume is not orthopedic. The largest group came for stellate ganglion blocks for PTSD, C-PTSD, dysautonomia, POTS or long COVID, several driving down from Vancouver BC or flying in, and they describe Wood spending an hour or more explaining the procedure before touching a needle. The regenerative injection reviews cover prolotherapy and PRP for decades-old back injuries, knees, shoulders and Ehlers-Danlos instability, and they single out his diagnostic ultrasound again and again. Libby, the practice manager and his wife, is named almost as often as he is. The criticism is narrow and consistent: two patients were left waiting an hour or had a follow-up pushed and never called back, one found the price around 30 percent above comparable providers and higher on the day than on the consult call, and a hip osteoarthritis patient reported 13 months of relief before progressing to bone on bone. Several reviews still use the practice's former name, Northwest Regenerative Orthopedics.
themes: stellate ganglion blocks for ptsd and long covid

highlights.author: Kerry L
highlights.text: I have just completed my prolotherapy sessions with Dr. Wood and I am beyond grateful for the incredible care that I have received at NW Regen. I have a back injury from over 25 years ago that left my fascia torn and tendons unstable, and most physicians told me there was nothing I could do about it. Dr. Wood provided me with a realistic expectation of what treatment may provide, but so far, my healing has exceeded every expectation and my back has a strength and stability that I have not felt in such a long time.

highlights.author: Jason-Laurie
highlights.text: I've been receiving prolotherapy injections for 17 years because I have a connective tissue disorder called Ehlers-Danlos. Dr. Wood is the 4th prolo/Platelet Rich Plasma doctor I have worked with in Oregon and is by far the best! His knowledge of anatomy and use of high tech ultrasound is able to accurately target the troubled areas. After dislocating the same knee 6 times, other doctors told me I needed a full knee replacement at age 42. However, after PRP & Stem Cell injections, I was able to avoid the knee surgery (and that was 7 years ago.)

highlights.author: Sheila
highlights.text: Unfortunately, neither scenario turned out to be true. I did have great pain relief for about 13 months, but then I started having problems again. I went to the orthopedic surgeon for an x-ray. I was now bone on bone with three bones spurs. The surgeon at Rebound said that stem cell/PRP wasn't ever going to work for my hip. The procedures are not covered by insurance, expensive and painful (at least in my experience.). It was basically expensive pain relief. If you have Osteoarthritis This may not be the right thing for you.

reddit.summary: No Reddit thread discusses this clinic. Searches on the brand name, on Dr. Wood, and on stellate ganglion block, prolotherapy and PRP providers around Portland return general discussion of the procedures plus one unanswered r/askportland request for an ultrasound-guided SGB doctor, with nobody naming NW Regen. There is no first-hand account of treatment here.
